title: PKM lead 1: F4 solving degree of the Kummer tower at m = 3, N = 21 and m = 4, N = 20
status_note: Blocked on hardware: the projection needs 133-146 GB (m = 3) and 243-384 GB (m = 4) of RAM against about 14 GB here, or a disk-backed B' reducer that is not built. The engine is pinned at the head of the open PR #1893. The engine has no checkpoint, so a run cannot resume; that must change, or the protocol must accept unresumable runs, before the card is ready.

links.lead: docs/ic/factor-base-encyclopedia/README.md §8 item 1 (is the tower's F4 solving degree bounded?)
notes: research/pkm_dickson_torus_20261015/README.md §5 on branch claude/leads-dickson-torus (Task C: derived, not run)

question: Does the Kummer tower's F4 solving degree D stay at 7 at m = 3, N = 21 (extending the plateau from N = 15 to L = 6 levels) and at m = 4, N = 20, or does it rise?
decision_value: This is the only open question in the PKM line that decides an exponent rather than a constant: a bounded solving degree is what would make a tower factor base sub-exponential to decompose against, and every other PKM card (the P-192 auxiliary-curve search, the P-224 depth checks) is worth running only if D is bounded. A rise to D = 8 at either cell is strong evidence against boundedness at that m and would deprioritise the tower constructions. A plateau at m = 3, N = 21 does not by itself establish H1a under rule A1 (that needs L > 10, i.e. N >= 27 at m = 3); it would justify the larger runs.

resources.notes: Derived (research/pkm_dickson_torus_20261015/README.md §5, not run): m = 3, N = 21: 133-146 GB, 2.5-7.4e15 multiply-adds, 86-138 h; m = 4, N = 20: 243-384 GB, 0.85-2.0e16 multiply-adds, 168-327 h; single-threaded at the round-7 rate, both cells 254-465 h. Too low if D rises 7 -> 8. The round-6 full-rank exit cuts time to about 0.61x and leaves memory unchanged. The kernel is rayon-parallel, so a many-core node shortens wall time roughly by core count.

params.argv_note: Flags follow research/pkm_dickson_torus_20261015/run.sh (p1 = 15*2^27 + 1, the prime of the recorded Kummer rows the projection extrapolates). The --budget and --max-nnz caps, and whether one or two targets per cell, are fixed in PROTOCOL.md.

outputs.result_schema: pkm_tower_pilot JSONL rows (one per (m, N, target): D, width, steps, multiply-adds, peak memory)

cairn.notes: Two single heavy runs: claim one task per cell, run it with `cairn lab exec` (receipt + rows published together), re-claim before the TTL lapses as the heartbeat, release completed or failed. Not preemptible: the engine cannot checkpoint, so a preempted run loses its work.
